summary: The note surveys indigenous art and culture festivals held since September 2023 that blend traditional heritage with modern technology and creativity. It covers dance, visual art, music, food, fashion, education and youth activism across events in New Mexico, Vancouver, Phoenix, Houston, California and Santa Fe. It concludes that these festivals show the resilience and adaptability of indigenous cultures and will keep growing.
one_line: Indigenous festivals since September 2023 reimagine tradition through technology-infused dance, art, music, cuisine, fashion, education and youth voices.
key_facts: The Mosaic Tradition Festival opened on September 5th, 2023 in New Mexico, spotlighting the cultural mosaics of the Navajo Nation.
Curator Eleanor Tsosie described the Mosaic Tradition Festival as "a revival through creativity."
Choreographer David Whitehawk said, "We dance to remember, but also to tell new stories. It’s about respect and evolution."
On October 12th at the Coastal Indigenous Arts Celebration in Vancouver, a troupe performed the Eagle Dance with LED-infused feathers.
At the Great Lakes Indigenous Art Fair (October 17th to 19th), Luna Papina showed pottery embedded with digital screens playing tribal oral histories.
Painter Jacob Running Bear unveiled interactive murals with touch-sensitive panels of tribal elders at the Desert Sky Art Symposium on November 3rd in Phoenix, Arizona.

At the Echoes of Heritage Music Festival in Houston, starting November 25th, flutist Aaron Two Rivers collaborated with electronic producer Haley Soundweaver, mixing traditional flute with ambient beats.
Chef Mariana Herrera presented "neoindigenous cuisine" at the Sun and Soil Festival in Sonora, California on December 8th.
Designer Michael Redfox showed avant-garde fashion inspired by cultural attire at the Skyloom Fashion Gala on December 21st.
At the Circle of Knowledge Festival in Santa Fe on January 18th, Theresa Blackowl taught basket weaving while Navajo technologist Jay Silverhorse led a drone class for youths.
17-year-old climate activist Emma Hollow Horn spoke at the Voices of Tomorrow Youth Summit, part of the Mosaic Tradition Festival, saying "Our ancestors gave us roots, but they also gave us wings."
